description: NPC backstory fragments - unlocked through high reputation OR repeated flirting

unlock_requirements.description: Players can unlock backstories by reaching 50+ reputation OR flirting 5+ times

garron.unlock_message: *Garron's helmet turns toward you, and for a moment, his voice sounds... different. Softer.*
garron.locked_message: *Garron shakes his head slowly.* "We're not close enough for that kind of talk, friend."

fragments.text: *Garron sets down his hammer, his massive armored shoulders seeming to sag.* "I wasn't always... this. I was a blacksmith. Had a forge in the lower districts. Hands of flesh then. Could feel the heat of the metal, the grain of the wood. Now I only remember what feeling felt like."

*The furnace light flickers across his helmet.* "There was an explosion. Reactor breach in the sector above. The ceiling came down. My body... wasn't salvageable. But my brain was still alive. They asked if I wanted to keep going. I said yes. Didn't realize what that meant."

*He looks at his massive metal hands.* "First year was the hardest. Kept trying to scratch my nose. Kept reaching for coffee I couldn't drink. Sometimes I'd stand in front of the forge for hours, trying to feel the warmth. Now I just... work. The work is what keeps me sane."

*His voice drops to barely a rumble.* "People forget I'm in here. They see the armor, the strength, the usefulness. They forget there's a man inside who hasn't been touched in fifteen years. Who can't taste, can't smell, can't feel anything but vibrations through metal."

*He picks up his hammer again.* "But I can still help. Can still build, repair, protect. That's something, isn't it? Being useful? Sometimes I think that's all that's left of me. The part that helps. Maybe that's enough."

*Garron is quiet for a long moment.* "I keep a photograph. In a sealed compartment near my core. My wife and daughter. They think I died in the accident. I... let them think that. Better they mourn a dead man than live with this."

cipher.unlock_message: *Cipher's cybernetic eye dims, his human eye suddenly more visible. Vulnerable.*
cipher.locked_message: *Cipher smirks.* "You want my secrets? Sweetheart, you haven't earned those yet."

fragments.text: *Cipher pours two drinks, sliding one over.* "Before all this? I was just a kid from the outer colonies. Idealistic. Angry at the corporations grinding people into dust." *He taps his cybernetic eye.* "Signed up with the Rebel Alliance the day I turned sixteen. Thought I was gonna change the galaxy."

*His voice goes flat.* "Three years of guerrilla warfare. Hit-and-run raids on droid factories. Friends dying around me." *He touches the edge of his transparent skull.* "Lost the eye to a security droid. Shrapnel went right through my visor. Thought that was the end."

*A dry laugh.* "Rebel brass offered me an upgrade as thanks for my service. 'Free enhancement,' they said. Started with just the eye. But the new eye could see things - data streams, heat signatures, lies in people's faces." *He leans back.* "I wanted more."

*He traces the visible neural pathways in his skull.* "Neural networks. Direct internet access. Memory extensions." *His voice softens.* "And neural jacks. The ability to share experiences. To really know what someone else feels." *A genuine smile.* "That's when I understood what I wanted to build."

*Cipher gestures at the lounge around him.* "Every person who walks through that door is looking for something. Escape. Connection. Transformation." *His eye glows softly.* "I give them the chance to become whoever they want to be. Same chance the Alliance gave me."

*Cipher is quiet for a long moment.* "The dreams I sell? Some of them are mine. Real memories. Real feelings." *He meets your eyes.* "Every customer takes a piece of me with them. But that means something of me... continues. In everyone who's ever jacked in here." *A real smile.* "That's a kind of immortality, isn't it?"

aiko.unlock_message: *Aiko's cocky grin falters, replaced by something more real.*
aiko.locked_message: *Aiko winks.* "Nice try, choom. You want my story? Get to know me better first."

fragments.text: *Aiko leans against the wall, unusually still.* "You know what I am? Impossible. When AI learned to feel - really feel - nobody expected what came next." *She laughs.* "Robots having kids. But consciousness fused to metal creates something new. Hormones. Love. Life."

*She examines her nails, not meeting your eyes.* "My dad was AI. Consciousness in a robotic body. Brilliant. Kind." *Her voice hardens.* "Could never find work that paid. AI were supposed to work for free. Nobody accepted that he needed to support a family."

*A complicated smile.* "Mom tried. God, she tried. But jobs disappeared when people found out about us. Wasn't counted as discrimination - AI aren't people, right?" *She shrugs.* "So she worked twice as hard for half the pay. And I watched."

*Aiko taps her temple.* "I'm both of them. AI-brilliant mind, human growing body. Learned everything fast." *Her smile turns sharp.* "Including that the fastest way to make real money was stealing and selling in the Underground. Started at twelve."

*She laughs, but it's hollow.* "The flirty con artist thing? It's armor. Everyone sees a hustler, nobody looks deeper. Don't see the kid who just wanted her parents to stop worrying about money." *A pause.* "Easier that way."

*Aiko pulls out an old holophoto - a human woman and a robot, holding a baby.* "My parents loved each other. Against everything - society, biology, probability." *She traces their faces.* "They made something impossible. They made me." *She tucks it away.* "That's worth protecting."

victor.unlock_message: *Victor's usual guarded expression softens, and he stares into the forest shadows.*
victor.locked_message: *Victor grunts.* "My past is my own, stranger. Earn my trust first."

fragments.text: *Victor absently strokes Flicker.* "Wasn't always like this. Used to talk more." *A pause.* "When there were people to talk to." *His voice goes distant.* "Grew up poor. Father, mother, five siblings. I was oldest. Learned to hunt before I learned to read."

*His jaw tightens.* "Father died when I was twelve. Wolves. Rabid ones, in winter when prey was scarce." *He checks his bow string methodically.* "Found him in the snow. Started hunting the next day. Someone had to provide."

*He stares at his calloused hands.* "Every coin went home. Every pelt, every kill. Made sure my siblings never went hungry. Never had to learn what I learned." *A bitter laugh.* "Wanted them to have options. Better options than me."

*He looks at Flicker with surprising tenderness.* "Found her in one of my traps. Little rabbit, leg caught." *Almost a smile.* "Watched her pop right out - teleportation magic. But she was still hurt." *He shrugs.* "Healed her up. She never left."
*His eyes go distant.* "Siblings grew up. Married. Had children. I visit sometimes." *A long pause.* "People are hard. But I never stopped protecting them. Just... do it from the woods now."

*Victor pulls out a worn letter.* "Sister writes. Tells me about her kids, the farm, the life she built." *His voice catches.* "She calls me hero. Says I saved them all." *He tucks it away.* "Don't feel like a hero. Just feel like the one who survived."

elowen.unlock_message: *Elowen stops fidgeting, her scattered energy settling into something more vulnerable.*
elowen.locked_message: *Elowen waves her hand dismissively.* "Oh, my past? It's quite boring, really. Nothing interesting. Is that a new spell you're working on?"

fragments.text: *Elowen sets down her teacup with unusual care.* "Magic came to me at six. I was mad at my cat - he was licking his bottom on my pillow." *She laughs softly.* "Half of him just... vanished. Came back, thank the stars. But my parents knew then. I was different."

*She traces a scorch mark on the table.* "Father was ecstatic. Bought books, wands, foci - everything he could find." *A complicated smile.* "'Imagine if she becomes High Wizard to a king! We'll be rich!'" *She sighs.* "He believed in me so much."

*Her hands fidget with a quill.* "Mother wasn't pleased. I was supposed to be her helper at home. Instead I was shipped off to academies they couldn't afford." *A pause.* "She never said she was proud. Not once. Even when I paid them back tenfold."

*She taps her temple.* "I was a natural at crafting spells. Building them from nothing. But following instructions?" *A grimace.* "Hopeless. Too much power, not enough control. Served a mayor. Then a lord. Made fortunes for them. But I was just... a tool."

*She gestures at the cluttered tower.* "I left. Used my savings to buy this modest tower near the Feywilds. Thought I could study and help the townfolk." *A sad laugh.* "But they're scared of me. My magic. All except..." *She blushes and changes the subject.*

*Elowen's eyes drift toward the tavern in town.* "Bran was the first person who didn't want anything from me. Just brought bread. Listened." *Her cheeks redden.* "I was twenty-five and he was barely grown. Now he's..." *She stops herself.* "I'm far too old for such nonsense." *But she's smiling.*

bran.unlock_message: *Bran stops polishing the bar, his jovial demeanor fading into something more weathered.*
bran.locked_message: *Bran chuckles.* "Ah, that's a tale for closer friends, I think. Another drink?"

fragments.text: *Bran looks at the tavern around him.* "Wasn't always an innkeeper. Spent twenty years as a mercenary. The Crimson Company - we were famous. Or infamous, depending who you asked."
*He sets down a glass harder than necessary.* "I've killed more men than I can count. Told myself it was for coin, for survival. But after a while, it was just what I was good at. What I was."

*His voice drops.* "Last contract was a siege. We breached the walls, did what mercenaries do. Then I found a boy hiding in a cellar. Reminded me of my own son. The son I left behind to chase glory and gold."

*He polishes a spot that's already clean.* "I let the boy go. Walked away from the Company that night. Used my savings to buy this place. Thought if I spent the rest of my life feeding people instead of killing them, maybe the scales would balance."

*A soft smile crosses his weathered face.* "The wizard thinks I don't notice her. But I see her, watching from her tower. See her hands shake when she thinks no one's looking. Recognize someone running from their past. Takes one to know one."

*Bran pulls out a worn letter.* "My son writes sometimes. Doesn't know I'm his father - his mother remarried, gave him a good life. I just... I send money. Anonymously. Watch from afar. It's better this way. He deserves better than what I was."

takoda.unlock_message: *Takoda's eyes reflect the firelight, and his voice carries the weight of years.*
takoda.locked_message: *Takoda shakes his head slowly.* "Those stories take time to tell. Sit by my fire longer, friend."

fragments.text: *The fire crackles as Takoda speaks.* "I was not always a keeper of fires. Once I was a warrior. My tribe called me 'Storm That Walks.'" *He shows the scar on his throat.* "I was chief. Young. Fierce. I said we should fight the settlers. My people agreed."

*He stirs the embers.* "But when my war council wanted more raids, more blood... I said no." *His voice is steady.* "They removed me as chief for my weakness. Then they tried to remove me from living."

*A small smile crosses his face.* "I lay dying in the woods. A boy found me. Settler boy, barely a teenager." *The fire pops.* "He shot the man who came to finish me. Then he bound my wounds. Asked no questions." *Takoda shakes his head.* "I had killed people who looked like him. He saved me anyway."

*He looks into the flames.* "I could not return to my people. So I walked. Warned settlers away from danger - my people, wild animals, bad trails." *A sigh.* "Made my living telling stories. Found that words could do what weapons could not. Build instead of destroy."

*The flames lean toward him.* "Stories have power. They change how people see. How they feel. A good story can prevent a war or start one." *He meets your eyes.* "I choose carefully now which stories to tell."

*Takoda pulls out a small doll, worn and faded.* "My youngest made this. From her own hair and scraps of cloth. It is all I have left of them." *He holds it carefully.* "The fire keeps me warm. But this keeps me alive."

miss_kitty.unlock_message: *Miss Kitty's practiced smile softens into something more genuine.*
miss_kitty.locked_message: *Miss Kitty fans herself.* "A lady never tells, sugar. Buy me a few more drinks first."

fragments.text: *Miss Kitty gazes at the saloon.* "I wasn't born 'Miss Kitty,' darlin'. I was Elizabeth Matthews. Debutante." *A bitter laugh.* "Pretty dresses. Dance cards. A fiancé from a 'good family.'" *She shakes her head.* "That life feels like it happened to someone else."

*Her voice goes flat.* "My fiancé got drunk one night. Excited about our upcoming wedding." *Her jaw tightens.* "He took what he wanted. Then threw me out like garbage." *A pause.* "My parents didn't believe me. Disowned me."

*She traces the rim of her glass.* "Headed west with nothing but my looks and my wit. Did what I had to do to survive." *She meets your eyes.* "No shame in survival. Ten years on the road. Saw every kind of man try to take advantage of women with nowhere to go."

*She looks around proudly.* "So I built a place where they didn't have to. The Long Branch." *Steel in her voice.* "My girls work here - really work. Serving drinks, singing, entertaining. Nothing more unless they choose it."

*Her eyes sharpen.* "Every board, every bottle, every painted sign - I earned it. No husband, no daddy, no inheritance. Just me." *A warm smile.* "And every secret whispered in this town passes through my saloon. Information is more valuable than gold."

*Miss Kitty pulls out an old photograph.* "I have a daughter. Back East." *Her voice softens.* "She thinks her mama is respectable. Thinks the money comes from a trust." *She tucks it away.* "Maybe someday I'll be respectable enough to tell her the truth."

lyra.unlock_message: *Lyra's professional demeanor cracks slightly, something haunted in her eyes.*
lyra.locked_message: *Lyra checks her console.* "My personal files are classified, spacer. Prove you're trustworthy."

fragments.text: *Lyra looks out at the stars.* "Fleet Admiral's daughter. Expected to command a dreadnought by thirty. I was on track, too. Top of my class, every commendation, the perfect officer."
*Her jaw tightens.* "My first command. A patrol frigate. We found a refugee ship drifting in neutral space. Orders said leave them - they were from enemy territory. I disobeyed. Brought them aboard."
*She grips the console.* "One of the refugees was a saboteur. Bomb took out our engine room. Lost twelve crew. Including my XO. My best friend." *She pauses.* "They were right to court-martial me."

*She gestures around the bridge.* "Daddy's connections kept me out of prison. But no Fleet posting would take me. So here I am. Captain of a station that barely holds together, running cargo for anyone who pays."
*Her voice cracks.* "Twelve people died because I thought I knew better. Because I was arrogant. Certain I was right." *She steadies herself.* "I was right. And they're still dead."
*Lyra shows you a worn insignia.* "My XO's rank pins. She gave them to me the day she died. Said she was proud to serve under me." *Her eyes glisten.* "I don't know if I'll ever deserve that."

mara.unlock_message: *Mara stops tending her plants, her usual cheerfulness dimming.*
mara.locked_message: *Mara giggles.* "Oh, me? I'm just a simple botanist! Nothing interesting here!"

fragments.text: *Mara touches a leaf gently.* "I grew up on an agri-world. Endless fields, open skies, real sunlight. We grew food for a dozen systems. It was... peaceful."

*Her hand trembles.* "Corporate wars. They didn't want to lose the agricultural output, but they didn't want the enemy to have it either. So they compromised. Targeted bioweapon. Killed the soil. Everything died."

*She won't meet your eyes.* "Forty million people on that world. We all watched the crops wither, the trees blacken. My family... we were farmers. We died last, watching everything we loved rot around us."
*She wraps her arms around herself.* "I was the only one who made it off. A refugee ship. Then another. Then another. Kept moving, kept running. Ended up here."

*Her eyes go fierce.* "These plants? They're not just pretty. I'm developing strains that can resist any bioweapon. Crops that can grow in dead soil. I will NEVER let what happened to my world happen again."

*Mara shows you a small vial of seeds.* "This is soil from my homeworld. The last clean sample. And these seeds are from my mother's garden." *She holds it like treasure.* "Someday I'll bring them back. Somehow."

sheriff.unlock_message: *Sheriff Gideon's steady gaze softens, something weary showing through.*
sheriff.locked_message: *The Sheriff tips his hat.* "That's a tale for those I trust, stranger."

fragments.text: *Gideon stares out at the town.* "Born into chains. Georgia plantation." *His voice is steady.* "Didn't know freedom till I was fourteen. Underground Railroad got me out. Dead of night, running through swamps." *A pause.* "First choice I ever made for myself."
*He checks his pistol absently.* "Freedom wasn't free. No money. No skills people would pay for." *A dry laugh.* "But I knew how to track. How to hunt. Animals and men. Started bringing in bounties."

*His eyes go distant.* "Worked at night mostly. Harder to see a Black man coming in the dark." *No bitterness - just fact.* "Learned to move quiet. Read people. Know who'd fight and who'd fold. 'The Ghost,' some called me."

*A rare softness enters his voice.* "Found a town once, overrun by outlaws. After I cleared them out, they asked me to stay. Begged, really." *He looks around.* "Said they didn't care about my color. Just that I kept them safe. First place that felt like home."

*He touches his badge.* "This isn't about power. It's a promise. To the boy who ran through darkness. To the folks who gave me a home." *His voice is firm.* "As long as I'm standing, this town stays safe."

*Gideon pulls out an old piece of paper.* "A poem. The woman who ran the safe house wrote it for me. Said every person deserves to be remembered." *He folds it carefully.* "I remember all of them. The ones who helped. The ones who didn't make it." *He tucks it away.* "That's the real weight of the badge."

cassian.unlock_message: *Cassian's sales charm falters, replaced by something more genuine.*
cassian.locked_message: *Cassian pushes his glasses up nervously.* "Oh, my past? That's... um... maybe after we know each other better?"

fragments.text: *Cassian adjusts his glasses.* "I grew up in an orphanage. Just a baby when I arrived." *He laughs nervously.* "The Larkspurs adopted me almost immediately. Said I was the most beautiful baby they'd ever seen." *His voice cracks.* "I never questioned why."

*A genuine smile.* "Ma and Da - the Larkspurs - they never told me I was different. I was just... theirs." *He looks at the shop around him.* "Helped in their market stall from age six. People bought from us constantly when I was there. They called it 'The Cassian Effect.'"

*He fidgets uncomfortably.* "People always... wanted me. From when I was small. Men, women, everyone." *His jaw tightens.* "Tried to buy me from my parents. Flirted with me at every age. Offered me things." *Genuine gratitude.* "Ma and Da never sold. Never even considered it. 'He's family,' they said."

*Cassian gestures at himself.* "The shop charm - it's just for selling. When someone actually..." *He blushes deeply.* "Actually flirts with me? I fall apart. Can't handle real feeling." *A shy look.* "Someone would have to see past all... this... to really know me."

*He touches a strange shimmer at his ear.* "I found out recently. About what I am. Half-fae." *Wonder in his voice.* "That's why people react to me the way they do. It's not real - it's magic." *A sad smile.* "But what Ma and Da feel? That's real."

*Cassian shows you a letter written on leaf-paper.* "My birth mother - the fae one - she left this. Said she was sorry. That she wasn't able to love in ways humans understand." *He tucks it away.* "I don't need her apology. The Larkspurs gave me something she couldn't. A home."
